https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2022/01.subtitle: Professor James Treadwell warns cancel culture ‘can happen to any of you’ after he is placed under investigation by Staffordshire University
https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2022/01.text:
A leading criminology professor has been placed under investigation by his university for “transphobia” after defending single-sex prisons.
Staffordshire University has launched a probe into Professor James Treadwell, an expert on crime and prisons, after receiving a complaint from an unknown source about his Twitter posts.
The scholar, who previously worked for the probation service, had expressed fears on social media that male sex offenders could access women’s prisons using loopholes designed for transgender inmates.
His comments backed an online “KeepPrisonsSingleSex” campaign, which has grown amid an unsuccessful House of Lords bid to place prisoners in facilities “by reference to their sex registered at birth”, rather than their gender identity.
Now Prof Treadwell, an executive member of the British Society of Criminology, has warned academics that being cancelled “can happen to any of you” and fears for his job.
Fellow professors leapt to his defence in the latest campus trans row.
Prof Treadwell made the following statement on Twitter:
He added: “Not only do I have no details of what it is alleged, I honestly have tried to be balanced and reasonable and promote fair debate. Let [me] be clear again, Trans people like all people deserve dignity and respect. Academics giving their personal views do too.”
The official transgender prison population has risen by a fifth in two years, standing at 197 last year.
Ministry of Justice rules allow inmates born male who identify as female to be kept in women’s prisons.
While the High Court ruled last year this policy was lawful, some academics and women’s rights groups are concerned that male sex offenders could exploit it, following several high-profile cases such as that of the abuser Karen White, who was jailed for life.
Prof Treadwell had tweeted before he announced the probe: “I do not think the main risk to women is not for the most part trans people, men or women, it is from men, using loopholes, but some of those come from pressure from the campaign from some (and not all, for it's hardly universal) transgender people."
He added that “over half of female prisoners have experienced sexual violence and abuse” and said he “cannot see any case for now why we should do anything but #KeepPrisonsSingleSex".
He has previously said male-born trans women should be kept in male estates because a “small number really do present a risk” in female-only wings.
Prof Jo Phoenix, another criminology lecturer who is suing the Open University after being compared to a racist for her views on gender in prisons, warned “the process is the punishment” in such probes.
"Criminology is a key discipline to help tease out the issues around prison placement policy for transgender prisoners," she said.
"This latest complaint shows a real determination on the part of a small minority to shut down legitimate discussion from academic experts where trans issues are concerned, especially where it calls into question the idea that self-declaration and self-identification are the only way to support the rights of transgender individuals, even in the prison context."
Prof Kathleen Stock, who left Sussex University after a bullying campaign by trans activists, said: “Accusations of transphobia have been weaponised in UK universities for several years now.
“If universities are serious about academic freedom, they need to adjust their internal processes so frivolous complaints like this don’t get the time of day. Nobody wants to be put through this and it is a deterrent to much needed research.”
The row comes after Lord Blencathra, the Tory peer, proposed an amendment to the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Bill to protect “exceptionally vulnerable” female prisoners by housing all inmates by the biological sex on their birth certificate, with separate facilities for trans inmates who identify differently. It was withdrawn this week.
A Staffordshire University spokesman said: “We can confirm we have received a complaint about views expressed by Prof Treadwell on Twitter.
“As we would do normally, this is in the process of being reviewed in accordance with the university’s procedures.
“As a university we are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion to ensure we promote a positive culture where everyone is able to be themselves. We are equally committed to academic freedom and lawful freedom of speech.
“We cannot comment any further at this stage.”
